listings.description: A family-owned Huron restaurant opened in 1979 by Albert and Roseanne Berardi and now in its fourth generation, serving scratch-made American, Italian and Lake Erie seafood dishes for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
listings.history: The Berardi family's food business began in 1942, when Eurosia "Mama" Berardi and her son Albert started selling fresh-cut french fries at the Midway at Cedar Point, working from Idaho potatoes and a hand-held potato peeler. The fries became as popular as the park itself and, in the family's telling, were a driving factor in the park's early days; they were sold there until Cedar Point stopped allowing private concessions in 1978. In 1979 Albert and Roseanne Berardi opened Berardi's Restaurant in Huron, focusing on fresh home-cooked food. It has remained family owned ever since and is now in the hands of the fourth generation, with many recipes in the family for more than three decades and nearly everything made from scratch.

listings.description: An Episcopal parish at 120 Ohio Street whose congregation has gathered since 1837, in the Episcopal Diocese of Ohio. It describes itself as "A Place of Grace" with a mission to "engage with Christ and our community to spread God's promise of hope, peace, joy, and love to the world."
listings.history: The Episcopal Society of Huron was organized in 1837 under the Rev. F. M. Levenworth, and the cornerstone of the present building was laid on 23 May 1838 — making it the oldest church building in Huron, standing near what had been the original southern limit of the village. The Rev. Samuel Marks became pastor in 1839 and served for over forty years. The building was added to the National Register of Historic Places on 4 March 1975 (reference no. 75001379), and the congregation marked its sesquicentennial in 1988.

listings.description: Bowling Green State University's regional campus, on a 250-acre site at One University Drive. One of BGSU's seven undergraduate colleges and its only campus outside Bowling Green, it teaches applied sciences, humanities, natural and social sciences, and College Credit Plus, and hosts outside events in its meeting spaces, auditoriums and the McBride Arboretum.
listings.history: BGSU Firelands was established in 1968 as Bowling Green State University's regional campus, about 60 miles north-east of the main Bowling Green campus, and it remains the university's sole regional campus. Its first dean was Dr. James H. McBride. When the campus was being developed in the late 1960s, McBride and his wife Margaret saw that the college held over 250 acres while only about a third was needed for buildings, and argued that the remainder "should be beautified for the edification, enjoyment, and education of all who would come." That became the James H. McBride Arboretum, established in 1983 as a partnership between BGSU and Erie Metroparks and named for him; it now holds over 200 species of flowers, trees and shrubs, with restored prairie plots, walking paths around Parker Lake and trails along Sawmill Creek.

listings.name: Huron Fire Division
listings.description: Huron's fire and EMS service, staffed around the clock from two stations. Most of its work is medical: 1,935 of 2,208 responses in 2025 were EMS calls.
listings.history: Huron's fire service was established in 1860 with hand-pumped equipment. In 1915 the village bought a horse-drawn ladder wagon from the City of Elyria, and local horse owners raced their teams to the station when the alarm sounded. Hank Schaffer was appointed the first fire chief in 1920 at $50 a year. Steam whistles served as the fire signal until 1923, when the city bought an electric siren for about $350. The first motorised apparatus, a Buffalo Larrabee pumper, arrived in 1925, followed by a Mack truck in 1934 that its crews nicknamed the "Blue Goose" for its blue paint. The division hired its first full-time firefighters in 1969 and bought its first ambulance the same year. In 1974 the station moved from the corner of Main Street and Jim Campbell Boulevard to the north end of Main Street. A fire levy in 1986 paid for four more full-time members and a 22-foot Boston Whaler rescue boat.
